title: The overnight gamble
desc: Why size, not the stop, protects you from gaps

cards.added: Common-sense opener on the p.73 gap explanation · Visual: Timeline: close $50 at 4 pm, news at 11 pm, open at 9:30 am
cards.name: After hours
cards.title: Closed for the night
cards.situation: You own a stock. It closes at $50 at 4 pm. At 11 pm, bad news comes out. Your broker trades regular hours only, 9:30 am to 4 pm. When can you sell?

options.feedback: It feels like the last price still holds. But after bad news, buyers set a new, lower price at the open.

options.text: At the open, at whatever buyers pay
options.feedback: Few people trade overnight, and your broker waits for the regular session. The first price you get is whatever buyers will pay at the open, often far below the close.
It feels like you can act the moment news comes out. But your broker only trades regular hours, so you can’t sell until the open.

cards.work: Closed at $50 − first trade at $45 = $5 loss a share.

cards.added: Illustrative gap: close $50, stop $48, open $45 (book p.73 explains gaps jumping stops in words)
cards.title: The gap that jumps your stop
cards.text: That overnight jump is a **[[gap|gap]]**. A stop only becomes a market order once the price trades at your level. Your stop is at $48, but the first regular-hours trade is $45. So you’re filled near $45, not $48. The stop can’t stop a gap.

chart.label: Closes at $50, then opens at $45 the next morning, below a stop at $48

visual.foot: Overnight gap: no trades between $50 and $45. Filled near {down}$45{/down}, not $48.

cards.added: Size slider interaction with worked numbers · Visual: Size slider drawn at $5,000 with the $500 and $50,000 stops (worked numbers added)
cards.title: Size decides the damage
cards.text: Same gap, $50 → $45, a −10% move. Your account: $5,000. Drag your position size and watch what the same gap costs you.

params.foot: You can’t stop a gap. You can choose your size.

cards.added: Worked numbers ($50, $625) added from the p.73 answer · Visual: Three-step sizing strip: budget $50 → gap 8% → size $625
cards.title: Think in risk, not in leverage
cards.text: Pros don’t ask “how much leverage?” They ask “if this goes wrong, **how much of my account do I lose?**” Pick a budget first: 1% of $5,000 = $50. Then size for a bad gap, not a normal one. Earnings gaps of 20% happen: $50 ÷ 0.20 = $250.

cards.name: Overnight gamble
cards.title: Earnings tonight
cards.q: You have $5,000. A friend says a stock will “definitely” jump after [[earnings|earnings]] tonight (the company’s results, a big-move day). Your broker offers 20×. The stock can gap 20% on earnings day. What do you do?

options.feedback: No leverage helps, but a 20% gap the wrong way still costs $1,000, a fifth of your account in one night.

options.text: $250 position, 1% at risk if it gaps 20%
options.feedback: A gap can jump past a stop, so size is your real protection: a 20% gap on $250 costs $50. A friend’s “definitely” isn’t a plan.
A “sure thing” makes big leverage tempting. But a 20% gap the wrong way loses far more than your account.
Less reckless, but a 20% gap the wrong way costs $5,000: your whole account in one night.

cards.title: Your real protection
cards.q: Why is position size, not a stop-loss, your real protection against an overnight earnings gap?

options.feedback: It doesn’t. A stop becomes a market order, so after a gap it fills at the opening price, which may be far past your level.
Brokers don’t cancel stops. The problem is the gap: the price jumps past your stop overnight.

options.text: A stop makes the gap bigger
options.feedback: Stops don’t cause gaps. News does. A stop just can’t control the price you get after a gap.

options.text: A gap can jump the stop; small size limits the hit
options.feedback: If the stock opens far below your stop, the stop fills at the open, not at your level. Only a small position keeps that loss small.

cards.headline: You can size a trade so one bad night can’t knock you out.
lines: Overnight gaps jump straight past stops.
Size for a bad gap: risk ÷ gap size.
Small size, not a stop, is your real protection.
